title: The Crause et al. (2007) pulsation ephemerides do not predict R Coronae Borealis decline onsets after 2006, and ASAS-SN onsets of 22 stars show no significant common pulsation phase
abstract: Question: Do decline onsets of R Coronae Borealis (RCB) stars occur at a fixed pulsation phase, as the ephemerides of Crause et al. (2007, CLH) state? Approach: We made a forward test of the fixed CLH ephemerides with the 17 later onsets of Percy & Dembski (2018) and one new ASAS-SN onset. We then measured the pulsation phase at onset for ASAS-SN (2014-2024) and ASAS-3 (2000-2009) declines of 167 VSX RCB stars. We calibrated the method with synthetic declines injected at random times into real data of the same stars. Results: The later onsets are not closer to the CLH ephemerides than random times (V-test p = 0.85; mean abs(O-C) 12.1 d against 10.7 d for random phases). Locking with 10 d scatter or less is rejected (p < 0.001). The early fade is slow (median 19 d from the first 0.15-mag departure to 1 mag). Thus a pulsation model fitted up to the onset puts onsets near minimum light: such a naive analysis of 52 real onsets gives p = 1.6e-7 against uniform phases, but p = 0.068 against injected declines. With a star period and a local fit that ends 20 d before onset (injected phase error 0.14 cycle), 27 onsets in 22 stars give Rayleigh p = 0.096 against the injection null, and variants give p = 0.19-0.72. We find no significant common phase. Limitations: the population test has power 0.75 for full locking with 0.1-cycle scatter, it cannot test a separate phase for each star (5 pairs), bright stars are saturated in ASAS-SN, and most RCB pulsation periods are poorly defined (8 of 35 agree with VSX within 10 percent). display.caption: O-C of decline onsets after the CLH data against the fixed CLH (2007) ephemerides. Circles: Percy & Dembski (2018) onsets (AAVSO visual). Star: our ASAS-SN onset of S Aps (2023). Open squares: last CLH onset of each star. Grey band: the +-10 d range that CLH reported. Dotted lines: +-P/2, the range of random phases. The later onsets fill the full range of random phases.

Pulsation phase at onset (0 = maximum light). (a) A pulsation model fitted up to the onset: declines injected at uniformly random times (grey) and real ASAS-SN onsets (red) both peak near minimum light, so the peak is a method bias. (b) Main method (star period, local fit that ends 20 d before the onset): real onsets (blue, ASAS-SN; green, ASAS-3) against the injection null (grey). Rayleigh p = 0.096.

Power of the population test against the fraction of phase-locked onsets, for intrinsic locking scatter of 0.05-0.20 cycle. Solid: probability of p < 0.05. Dotted: probability that the statistic is not larger than the observed value. (a) One phase for all stars (27 onsets). (b) A separate phase for each star (5 same-star pairs): the data cannot test this case.

citations.reason: Crause, Lawson & Henden (2007): linear decline-onset ephemerides tied to the pulsation periods of five RCB stars. We use their periods and test the ephemerides forward; later onsets are not closer to them than random times.

Percy & Dembski (2018): onset times after the CLH data and the CLH zero points (Table 1), and RY Sgr onset-minus-maximum times (Table 4). We use these values; our formal test does not support their statement that the onsets stay locked.

Crawford et al. (2025): largest RCB decline study; no onset periodicity in Fourier spectra except RY Sgr, Poisson onsets for R CrB and SU Tau. Our forward test and calibrated phase test agree and add a power analysis.
Percy (2019): ASAS-SN pulsation periods of RCB stars, used as context for period uncertainty.
Feast et al. (2019): no coherent pulsation in R CrB radial velocities. Our period comparison and injection phase errors agree that most RCB pulsations are poorly coherent.
Hart et al. (2023): ASAS-SN Sky Patrol v2, source of the 2014-2026 light curves and of the VSX table query.
Kochanek et al. (2017): ASAS-SN light-curve server and photometry.
Pojmanski (2002): ASAS-3 photometry, source of the 2000-2009 light curves.
Watson et al. (2006): AAVSO VSX, source of the RCB star list and catalogue periods.
Campaign result that documented ASAS-SN Sky Patrol v2 single-camera null-flux artefacts; we use a cross-camera and sustained-fade veto because of it.
DREAMS RCB monitoring pages with ATLAS forced photometry; suggested data for a denser follow-up test (not used).
